gap: No result ChatGPT got gives ENERGY STAR's lab-certified figures for any candidate. The Brio 500 Series (CLBL520SC), Brio Moderna (CLBL720SC) and Brio 400 (CLBL420V2) share one certification: 0.76 kWh/day with no water drawn, 42°F cold water, 167°F hot water and 0.74 gal/h cold capacity. Avalon, maker of ChatGPT's value pick, the A4, has 0 of the 191 ENERGY STAR-certified water coolers.
standout_why: I compared against Bob Vila (cited), Shouldit and mybest. Bob Vila gives only 1–5 tester scores, an A4 heat time of about 5 minutes and a general line that ENERGY STAR coolers use about 30% less energy, with no figure for any model. Shouldit measured hot-water temperature, cold output per hour and flow for Avalon A4, A1, A5, A8 and Frigidaire EFWC519, but reports no energy use and no measured cold temperature, and it tested no Brio or Primo. mybest reports no test numbers. No page says which candidates are ENERGY STAR certified or gives kWh/day, and none notes that the Brio 500 and Moderna share one certification. Popular Mechanics blocked fetching, so I could not check it.
decides: This confirms Brio 500 Series (CLBL520SC, $329.99 at briowater.com on 2026-11-10) as the measured, certified pick. The Moderna (CLBL720SC, $341.99 on ChatGPT's card) appears under the same ENERGY STAR record, so its premium buys adjustable temperatures, not certified efficiency or chilling. The Avalon A4 value pick has no ENERGY STAR certification to cite. A shopper who wants a certified-efficient budget unit should look at Brio's own lineup or Primo (for example 601202 / 601088 family, 0.76 kWh/day, 42°F). Shouldit's own measurements of the Avalon A4 (199°F hot, 183 fl oz/h cold) are still the best data on the A4.
